newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hafslund eyes east Europe power trade.
newsitem.headline: Hafslund eyes east Europe power trade.

text.p: Norwegian power producer Hafslund ASA said on Tuesday it had entered a cooperation agreement with Petrol Holding and had acquired 50 percent of the shares in Norwegian Oil Trading Holding AS.
Petrol Holding is a privately-owned Norwegian holding company with activities in oil and energy trading and power production.
Hafslund said the stock was bought through a private placing of 49.25 million crowns. The remaining 50 percent of shares in Norwegian Oil Trading will remain with Petrol Holding, it said.
"Hafslund is positioning itself for electricity trading in eastern Europe," the statement said.

Norwegian Oil Trading has traded in eastern Europe since 1984, mainly in the crude oil and bunker markets. Operating revenues in 1996 were 938 million crowns with operating profits amounting to 8.2 million crowns.
The company has 12 employees, mainly in Norway, and recently opened an office in Minsk, Belarus.

"In addition to the present area of operation, the company will search for business opportunities within the power market," Hafslund said. "The power market in east Europe is changing, which gives possibilities for future trade within the region and increased east-west trade," it said.
